Learning new things used to be a thrill for me, but now, as a software engineer, it has become a chore. I spend nearly every waking moment studying new shit, none of the shit from before is applicable to what I need to do now. This is especially a problem in front-end design. The user interface world seems to adopt new frameworks faster than I can discover their names. I'm learning two languages because my coworkers primarily speak Chinese and my wife speaks Japanese (although she is fluent in English too, I wish I could connect with her on another level) I feel like I am perpetually an ameteur, denied to opportunity to master anything. What do you recommend to stay ahead of this flood?

What about you greybeards out there? what do you do?
What should I do to learn faster?
Get more sleep. Your brain needs time to process and comprehend. And don't assume it needs to all be at night. Naps are awesome way to increase memory retention and raise awareness.
Good point. I have never really napped, but could give it a try.

As you stated, new frameworks and libraries come out all the time. I think it's good practice to chose one and go with it for a while. This means you will need to select one that is relatively new but adopted by many. React is a good example.

New development happens all the time when using a new-ish framework/library, but it all conforms to the original concept defined by the framework. This way you aren't throwing out what you already know but you can continue to learn new ideas.

Regarding always feeling like an amateur, I think that's kind of the life of a software (especially web) engineer. You need to be on your toes at all times since software development moves fast. It's exciting for many, but not for everyone.

Just my 2 cents.

I definitely find it exciting to make an interface that really serves the users needs and is as simple as possible, and I'll use whatever is suited to the task. But sometimes I wish there was a javascript czar who could just say everybody use X for everything from now on and everyone caught inventing other ways of doing things will be shot. 3 years would go by and then everyone would be able to make a decent UI in an hour just like everyone understands how to use folders and the clipboard.

You sound like you are worn out and have possibly lost the passion you once had in you're chosen field.

My advice would be toke sure you get more rest and more quality "you" time; spend time pursuing hobbies or activities not directly related to work.

"All work and no play makes Jack a dull boy"

Bloody hell dude, you need to focus. You're learning Chinese and Japanese at the same time? You've got the mental capacity to do whatever you want, no question. Just not the capacity to do everything. Oh, and why are you learning shit you can't use later? Try taking a step back and considering what your specific goals actually are.
Get in the zone, get some nice beats, pep yourself up and charge into battle.

Meditate. Seriously. It helps. Just turn off for a bit.

Also, when you learn something new, try and imagine in your head that you have to teach it to someone else. See what bits trip you up and cover them again. it's like rubber duck programming, but sort of "rubber duck explaining it to myself as personal revision".

And sleep. Proper sleep. Cut out caffeine if you can. It will suck for a few days/a week, depending on your current in-take, but it will help in the long run.

Elizabeth Bathory believed that young virgin blood was the solution for eternal youth and beauty.
